clips.caption:
John D. Rockefeller was the richest man who had ever lived, and on his deathbed, he was still working on making more money. A reporter asked him the obvious question: how much more do you need? With tears in his eyes, he said, 'just a little more.'

The richest man in the world, and it was never enough — because what he was actually chasing was never in the money to begin with. It was the feeling of being whole, and that was available the entire time, free, already inside him.

Comment RISE and I'll send you where that feeling actually comes from.

clips.end_words: This is how it's been always
clips.caption:
In ancient Egypt, only the priests were allowed near the gods. In Judaism, only the Levites could enter the holy of holies. In Catholic practice, you still confess to a priest instead of speaking to God directly — he's the intermediary, the one who hands your forgiveness back to you.

Same structure, every era, every religion: someone positions themselves between you and the source, and once you believe you need them, you never leave. You didn't need a middleman then, and the part of you that's actually divine doesn't need one now either.

Comment RISE and I'll send you how to go direct.
